sources: Horowitz 2009, Behavioural Processes (abstract): 14 dogs videotaped; owners gave a command not to eat a treat and left the room; trials "varied the owners' knowledge of what their dogs did in their absence"; "no difference in behaviours associated with the guilty look"; "more such behaviours were seen in trials when owners scolded their dogs"; "The effect of scolding was more pronounced when the dogs were obedient, not disobedient"; the look "is a response to owner cues, rather than that it shows an appreciation of a misdeed"; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/19520245/

Ostojic, Tkalcic & Clayton 2015, Behavioural Processes: "Ninety-six owners and their dogs were tested in Croatia"; "owners stated that their dog had eaten the food no more than expected by chance"; "dogs' greeting behaviours were not affected by their own action or the presence or absence of the food"; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4310318/

Hare, Brown, Williamson & Tomasello 2002, Science (abstract): "domestic dog puppies only a few weeks old, even those that have had little human contact, do show these skills" (following human pointing to find food); https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12446914/
Scheider, Kaminski, Call & Tomasello 2013, Animal Cognition (abstract): "Dogs ignored the human's gesture if they had better information"; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/23138936/

Muller, Schmitt, Barber & Huber 2015, Current Biology (abstract): "dogs for which the happy faces were rewarded learned the discrimination more quickly than dogs for which the angry faces were rewarded"; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25683806/

Andics et al. 2016, Science (abstract): "increased activity in primary reward regions only when both lexical and intonational information were consistent with praise"; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27576923/

beats.say: That guilty fucking look on your dog may not be a confession.
You know the face. Like it just robbed a fucking bank.
In 2009, a researcher videotaped 14 dogs to test it. For science, and for fucking treats.
The setup: the owner says don't eat the treat, then leaves the room. Fucking classic.
Result one. Whether they ate it or not, the guilty look was no different. What the fuck.
Result two. The look showed up more when owners scolded. Well, fuck.
And the effect was bigger in dogs that obeyed. Unfair as fuck.
The researcher's read: it's better described as a response to owner cues, not proof of guilt. Plot fucking twist.
That doesn't mean dogs feel nothing. The test was about the look, not the fucking feelings.
In 2015, another team tested 96 dogs. Bigger fucking sample.
Owners guessed from the greeting whether their dog ate the food. No better than chance. A fucking coin flip.
The dogs' greeting didn't change either. No fucking tells found.
Here's the shit dogs can fucking read in tests.
Your signals. Puppies a few weeks old read them to find hidden food. Tiny fucking geniuses.

beats.say: But no blind following. In one test, dogs that knew better ignored the fucking finger.
Faces, too. Dogs rewarded for the happy face learned faster than for the angry one. Fair as fuck.
In a brain scanner, reward areas lit up only when the word and the tone both meant praise. Praise in a flat voice didn't fucking light them up.
So that face over the chewed shoe? It may be answering you, not confessing. Fuck knows.
So: does your dog do the face? Be fucking honest.
